name: smartctl

storage.rationale: smartctl is a one-shot reader with no daemon and no state directory; it writes nothing outside the invoking workflow. The explicit empty declaration records that.

description: SMART attribute reader (smartmontools) — reports storage wear, reallocated and pending sectors, media errors and power-on hours for the system-monitor device graph
installHint: Install smartmontools via your package manager. Presence on PATH is not sufficient: smartctl must open the raw block device. `vrooli setup` installs the tool but does not grant persistent access to system-monitor. For a one-time identity-bound diagnostic, use `vrooli host volume smart --device <whole-disk> --serial <expected-serial>`; the control-plane broker rechecks the serial and runs only `smartctl -j -H -A`. This does not grant ongoing raw-device access to scenarios; their SMART telemetry remains unmeasurable when device permissions deny access. Windows uses Get-StorageReliabilityCounter instead.
notes: Peer to rasdaemon: rasdaemon is the primary for memory and PCIe error telemetry, smartctl covers the storage half. Consumed by scenarios/system-monitor/api/internal/devicegraph/smart.go, which parses the -j output for both the NVMe health log and the ATA attribute table.

windows.evidence: This host OS has no declaration for the provider native command surface.
